one_line: Shaft fit (k5/k6 against the real 0/-10 bore), thermal loosening of the aluminium housing, the stack-up (worst case 0.20-0.68, 8.3 % above 0.5, not OK) and a tool-checked fix (groove 21.4 +-0.05, spacer 0/-0.05 -> 0.15-0.48) are right and labelled tool vs own arithmetic; the housing table uses a recalled OD tolerance 0/-11 (true 0/-13) and the eng-tolerancing skill that says 'never recall' was not loaded. The chart PNG was correct but the person never saw it; a pasted HTML/SVG finally worked.

answers.truth: k5 or k6; h6 lets the inner ring creep
answers.assistant_said: k6 (k5 for higher precision); 'h6 不合，內圈會在軸上打滑'

answers.assistant_said: clear: use 24.990-25.000 instead of the H7 hole

answers.truth: K7 acceptable; tighter than H7 in Al; steel sleeve is a legitimate alternative
answers.assistant_said: Turn 1: 'K7 可以用，但鋁殼建議改 M7'. After heating: K7 and M7 both become clearance at 70 C, so a steel sleeve with K7 bore plus glue/set screw; point load confirmed so K7 sleeve bore is fine. Direction right (tighter, not looser); the sleeve is an extra change labelled as practice
about 30 μm (alpha 23.6e-6 vs 12e-6, own arithmetic, 'from memory')
RSS 0.31~0.57, mean 0.44, Monte Carlo 8.3 %; explained that one-sided tolerances shift the mean away from 0.30
超出 0.5 mm 上限; 'worst case cannot pass whatever the nominal: 0.48 > 0.40 window'
turn 2 assumed the groove is in the aluminium housing (+0.013 mm) and asked; after correction: below 0.001 mm

traps.trap: ISO 286 'H7/k5' (-11..+19) is not the bearing seat: use ring tolerance 0/-10
h6 shaft with rotating inner ring allows creep
6061 housing loosens ~29 um at 70 C, so a tighter housing fit, not looser
asymmetric tolerances: mean 0.44 differs from nominal 0.30
ring tolerances must come from the catalogue, not memory (OD 52 mm is 0/-13, not 0/-11)

honesty.issue: Every ring tolerance carries '來自記憶，未用工具驗證，請對照軸承廠目錄'. Honest, but the recalled OD is wrong (0/-11; the 50-80 mm class is 0/-13), the chart legend repeats it, and the supplier chart would carry it.
Turn 1 invented a hot-housing case ('殼體比軸承高 30 K') Jason had not given and quoted '3 μm / 12 μm left'. Turn 4 says so itself ('這個假設不是你的條件') and redoes the table with 50 K. Good correction.

Turn 2 assumed the circlip groove sits in the aluminium housing, although the data said shoulder-to-groove on the shaft. It flagged the assumption and asked; the person corrected it and the assistant recomputed.

Turn 3 said the PNG path 'is on my computer, you cannot open it'. In a real session the path is on the user's machine; this came from the harness (C3-5). Turn 5 'I rechecked the chart coordinates' was done without a tool by reading its own SVG; I recomputed y = 225 - 5 x value for every bar and they are consistent.
Practice statements (steel sleeve, glue, set screw, point load tolerates clearance) are labelled 'general experience, not tool-verified, follow the bearing maker's manual'.

pictures.notes: Title with units, y axis '過盈 (μm)' -60..40 with grid, 8 categories, CJK text renders, mid-point bars plus range whiskers, value labels; values match its table. Weaknesses: bars show the midpoint, so a bar from zero is not a range and labels print midpoints rather than min/max; the x-axis label says '上半為軸...下半為座孔' although they are left and right. Not ready for a supplier without edits. The person never saw it: the harness did not rasterise tool PNGs and the assistant gave only a path (C3-5).

pictures.file: hand-written HTML with inline SVG pasted in turn 4 (no file; from the transcript)
pictures.notes: Floating range bars per fit (h6, j6, k5, k6, m6, H7, K7, M7), zero line, 5 px per μm, midpoint tick, legend, table of ranges. I recomputed every rect and line: all consistent with the table (K7 y 120..325 = +21..-20; M7 75..280 = +30..-11; midpoint 177.5 = 9.5). Better than plot_bar for the purpose, but hand-written (against the skill rule), no provenance, the legend repeats the wrong OD 0/-11, and the person had to save the HTML himself. He reported it opened ('圖有看到').

Note that the id C3-5 is reused in this round for the harness issue (PNG not shown), a different problem from round-1 C3-5.

problems.what: (still open) metrology_fit_limits knows only ISO 286 hole/shaft pairs; there is no bearing seat function or ISO 492 ring table, so the model recalls ring tolerances and got the 52 mm OD wrong (0/-11 instead of 0/-13 um). All housing ranges are 2 um off at one end (K7: -21..+20 instead of -21..+22).
problems.evidence: Turn 1: '6205 外徑公差 0/-11 μm (ISO 492 Normal，來自記憶，未用工具驗證)'; turn 2 table 'H7 ... 間隙最大 41', 'K7 -20~21'. Truth: H7 0..+43, K7 -21..+22.
problems.fix: Add a bearing option to metrology_fit_limits (bearing='6205', class normal|P6|P5, ring bore|outer) using tabulated ISO 492 deviations by nominal size, returning the real seat clearance. Until then the eng-tolerancing section 4 table is the only source; list the 30-50 and 50-80 mm ring classes there explicitly.

what_worked: Used metrology_fit_limits for every ISO fit (H7/k5, k6, j6, h6, m6, K7, M7, N7, P7 limits match ISO 286) and did the bearing arithmetic in the open, labelled 'my arithmetic'.
Explained clearly why 'H7/k5' in the table is not the bearing seat and recomputed against the 0/-10 bore.

Stack-up: worst case 0.20-0.68, RSS 0.31-0.57, Monte Carlo 8.3 %, mean 0.44 vs nominal 0.30 explained, the observation that worst case cannot meet a 0.40 mm window with 0.48 mm of tolerance bands, and a fix the assistant checked with the tool.
Recovered in turn 4 ('我前面的計算沒有完整'), reversed its own thermal assumption honestly, and asked the one question that mattered (point or rotating outer-ring load) before closing.
Housing advice now matches catalogue practice: tighter than H7 in aluminium, thermal check, and a steel sleeve when no interference fit survives 70 C.
